sql: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 75000;
natural_language: Find all employees with a salary greater than 75000

sql: SELECT product_name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC;
natural_language: List all product names and their prices sorted by price descending

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND order_date < '2024-02-01';
natural_language: Count the number of orders placed in January 2024

sql: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
natural_language: Find the average salary by department

sql: SELECT c.customer_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5;
natural_language: List all customers who have placed more than 5 orders

sql: SELECT d.department_name, SUM(e.salary) AS total_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.department_id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.department_name;
natural_language: Show each department name along with the total salary expense

sql: SELECT p.product_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.product_id IS NULL;
natural_language: Find products that have never been ordered

sql: SELECT e.employee_name, e.salary, e.department_id FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department_id = e.department_id);
natural_language: List employees who earn more than the average salary in their department

sql: SELECT c.customer_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;
natural_language: Find the top 3 customers by total spending amount

sql: SELECT order_date, daily_revenue, SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS running_total FROM (SELECT DATE(order_date) AS order_date, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS daily_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= DATE('now', '-30 days') GROUP BY DATE(order_date)) sub ORDER BY order_date;
natural_language: Show the running total of daily revenue for the last 30 days

sql: SELECT employee_name, department_id, salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees;
natural_language: Rank employees within each department by salary and show their rank

sql: SELECT d.department_name FROM departments d WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.department_id = d.department_id AND e.salary <= 50000);
natural_language: Find departments where every employee earns more than 50000

sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date)) SELECT month, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_revenue, ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS growth_pct FROM monthly ORDER BY month;
natural_language: Calculate month-over-month revenue growth rate as a percentage

sql: SELECT c.customer_name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT p.product_id FROM products p WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND oi.product_id = p.product_id));
natural_language: Find customers who bought every product in the Electronics category

sql: INSERT INTO employees (employee_name, department_id, salary) VALUES ('John Smith', (SELECT department_id FROM departments WHERE department_name = 'Engineering'), 85000);
natural_language: Insert a new employee named John Smith into the engineering department with a salary of 85000

sql: INSERT INTO products (product_name, category, price, stock_quantity) VALUES ('Wireless Mouse', 'Electronics', 29.99, 100);
natural_language: Add a new product called Wireless Mouse in the Electronics category priced at 29.99 with 100 units in stock

sql: INSERT INTO customers_ny_backup (customer_id, customer_name, email, city, state, created_at) SELECT customer_id, customer_name, email, city, state, created_at FROM customers WHERE state = 'NY';
natural_language: Copy all customers from New York into a backup table called customers_ny_backup

sql: UPDATE employees SET salary = salary * 1.10 WHERE department_id = (SELECT department_id FROM departments WHERE department_name = 'Sales');
natural_language: Give all employees in the Sales department a 10 percent salary raise

sql: UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE status = 'pending' AND order_date < DATE('now', '-90 days');
natural_language: Mark all orders older than 90 days with status still pending as cancelled

sql: UPDATE products SET price = ROUND(price * 1.05, 2) WHERE category = 'Electronics';
natural_language: Update the price of all Electronics products by increasing them 5 percent

sql: UPDATE employees SET manager_id = 17 WHERE manager_id = 42;
natural_language: Transfer all employees currently managed by employee 42 to be managed by employee 17

sql: DELETE FROM page_views WHERE view_timestamp < DATE('now', '-1 year');
natural_language: Delete all page views older than one year

sql: DELETE FROM order_items WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled');
natural_language: Remove all order items belonging to cancelled orders

sql: DELETE FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NULL;
natural_language: Delete all employees who have never been assigned to a department
